# Bug report: frequent pollers get locked out

`limiter.py` implements a per-client token-bucket rate limiter used by our API gateway.

Support tickets say: clients that call the API often (several times per second) stay rate-limited
long after they slow down, even though their average rate is well under their limit. Clients that
call rarely are fine.

Fix the bug(s) in `limiter.py`. Keep the public API exactly the same (class names, method names,
arguments, return values). Do not add dependencies. `example.py` shows typical usage.
CLAUDE.md
TASK.md
example.py
limiter.py

content.text:
Fixed in `limiter.py`: `Bucket.refill` computed `int(elapsed * self.rate)` and still advanced `self.last`. A client calling every 0.1s at 2 tokens/s earned 0.2 tokens per call, which truncated to 0, so the fractional refill was thrown away every time. I removed the `int()`, so tokens are now fractional. The public API is unchanged.

I checked it with a quick throwaway script using a fake clock. After the burst was exhausted, 20 calls at 0.1s spacing were allowed exactly 4 times, which matches the 2/s rate. I didn't add a permanent test file.

One thing to know: `stats()` now returns fractional token counts instead of whole numbers.
